entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Laodice I was a Greek noblewoman of Anatolia who played a crucial role in shaping the early Seleucid dynasty. As the first wife of King Antiochus II Theos, Laodice I managed to secure her family's interests and influence through strategic marriages and alliances.

Born into a prominent family in Pergamon, Laodice I was well-educated and had close ties with influential figures like Eumenes II of Pergamon. Her marriage to Antiochus II Theos brought significant wealth and power, allowing her to promote the interests of her family and protect their territories.

Laodice I's legacy extends beyond her own lifetime, as her descendants continued to play a prominent role in the Seleucid Empire. Her influence can be seen in the reigns of subsequent kings, including Antiochus III Theos and Seleucus IV Philopator. The impact of Laodice I's strategic marriages and alliances also influenced the rise of Pergamon as a major power in the ancient world.

Despite her significance, Laodice I remains somewhat of an enigma, with many details about her life and reign still shrouded in mystery. Nevertheless, her story serves as a testament to the enduring power of women's agency in shaping the course of history.
